<summary>

  <learned>The pageOffset calculation had an off-by-one error where it was subtracting 1 from the page index before multiplication, causing the first page to start at an incorrect offset. The correct formula is (page * size) to calculate the offset.</learned>
  <completed>Applied edit to OrderQuery.pageOffset method to remove the extra -1 from the calculation. OrderQueryTest#firstPageStartsAtZero now passes, confirming the fix resolves the pagination issue.</completed>
  <next_steps>Bugfix is complete with passing test coverage. No further immediate work indicated for this pagination issue.</next_steps>
  <notes>This was a classic off-by-one error in pagination logic. The fix ensures page 0 correctly starts at offset 0, page 1 at offset size, etc. Test coverage validates the expected behavior.</notes>
</summary>

<summary>
  <request>Fix race condition in UserCache where concurrent callers could both write null placeholders</request>
  <investigated>The UserCache.get method was examined and found to have a concurrency issue where two simultaneous callers could both write null placeholder values due to a lack of atomic load-on-miss behavior.</investigated>
  <learned>UserCache.get previously did not use computeIfAbsent, allowing a race window where multiple threads could independently attempt to load cache entries, resulting in duplicate or null placeholder writes under concurrent access.</learned>
  <completed>The UserCache.get method was refactored to use computeIfAbsent for cache loading, ensuring that concurrent callers are serialized per-key and cannot both write a null placeholder. The CacheConcurrencyTest now passes, confirming the fix resolves the race condition.</completed>
  <next_steps>No additional work has been requested at this checkpoint; awaiting further instructions or new tasks from the user.</next_steps>
  <notes>This is a minimal-change concurrency fix using Java's ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent semantics to guarantee single-threaded initialization per cache key.</notes>
</summary>

<summary>
  <request>Fix race condition in UserCache and verify the fix</request>
  <investigated>Inspected src/main/java/com/acme/cache/UserCache.java to identify the concurrency bug</investigated>
  <learned>UserCache.get was using cache.get(id) which allowed two concurrent callers to both write a null placeholder, causing a race condition</learned>
  <completed>Applied fix changing cache.get(id) to cache.computeIfAbsent(id, loader::load), which ensures atomic loading. CacheConcurrencyTest now passes.</completed>
  <next_steps>Run the full verification suite to ensure no regressions</next_steps>
  <notes>The fix uses computeIfAbsent to guarantee that only one thread can load a value for a given id, eliminating the race condition with null placeholders</notes>
</summary>

  <next_steps>The race condition fix is complete and tested. Session may continue with additional tasks or verification.</next_steps>
  <notes>The test result confirms the fix resolves the concurrent increment issue. AtomicLong.incrementAndGet is the idiomatic solution for atomic counter operations in Java.</notes>
</summary>
